An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into two segments, above 4.0 PeV and above 16.0 PeV, and conducted separate analyses on each. Both divisions exhibited distinct annual periodicities along with distinct modulation amplitudes, featuring specific solid angles and varying dipolar components. Notably, both segments showed consistent annual variation patterns and shared similar geometrical modulation components, perhaps, indicating a common extraterrestrial origin. Nevertheless, both segments exhibited distinct non-common origin aspects, possibly, reflecting different influences related to our solar system's interaction with the local interstellar environment. Moreover, both divisions exhibited different signals of longitudinal and directional anomalies, affecting the intensity and composition of extremely energetic particle events, respectively.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are indicated by non-Gaussian characteristics in specific angle distributions and by new patterns in higher-order correlations that increase with collision centrality. Importantly, both methods used to measure these fluctuations give consistent results. Furthermore, these fluctuations increase with lower energy transfers in collisions and move to less extreme values as collisions become more central. They also move to less extreme values as collisions become more central

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches, we consider a more comprehensive set of inconsistencies, encompassing violations of integrity rules beyond the most basic ones. We examine various types of inconsistencies arising from a wide range of functional dependencies, including those that may be partially unknown. To address this issue, we develop an algorithm rooted in graph theory, specifically a modified version of Tarjan's algorithm, to efficiently uncover these dependencies. Furthermore, we create an incremental version of the algorithm, allowing it to adapt when new data is added or existing connections are discovered. To validate our approach, we implemented the algorithm and conducted valuable case studies using both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This study presents a novel Poisson autoregressive model with time-varying coefficients, bridging the gap between constant coefficient models and volatile threshold models. It also develops consistent estimators and reliable confidence intervals for model parameters, initially using the oracle device to obtain initial parameter estimates, then employing consistent methods for estimating standard errors.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose whose descriptor corresponds to that in the demonstration. NDFs
are efficiently trained without expert input using a self-supervised approach,
and provide a robust object understanding invariant to frame of reference, and
equipped with variance estimation. NDFs demonstrate a 20% enhancement in task
generalization compared to PointNet features.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these earlier results have a larger systematic uncertainty.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, as well as to identify a threshold beyond which an algorithm known as Gradual Activation is guaranteed to remain within a convex region. Additionally, we found that our inequality can replace previous methods for ensuring the algorithm enters a convex area. However, it is not possible to prove that this algorithm always enters a convex area, as indicated by specific counterexamples.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined quickly, regardless of the system's absolute calibration, and even provides calibration as a by-product. Our team used extensive data from the FRAM telescope at the Pierre Auger Observatory and a similar telescope at the Cherenkov Telescope Array site to improve the precision of this method to a precision of possibly 0.01. To accomplish this, we conducted precise laboratory measurements of the system's response to varying light intensities and spectra to counter the limitations of non-linear CCD detectors under observation conditions.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained considerable interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters in the initial stage, followed by utilizing these cues to refine the 6D pose in the second stage through optimization. Researcher studies have primarily concentrated on estimating world-centered projection (WCP) and local-centered projection (LCP) in the second stage, neglecting one crucial projection known as the Body-Centered Projection (BCP). Nevertheless, projection under BCP conditions pose challenges due to its inherently unstable nature. In response to this issue and building on our earlier work, we introduce DeepHMap++, which not only differentiates and separates the training of WCP and LCP projections but also differentiates and separates the training of BCP projection by training it independently with a distinct projection group. By distinguishing and separating the training of projection features, DeepHMAP++'s approach allows the network to focus on specific features of each projection type, enabling more effective learning. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that DeepHMAP++'s performance surpasses that of previous models which trained projection features without distinction and two-stage methods in multiple datasets.

Python is widely used due to its simplicity and extensive library support, making it popular in statistics and machine learning. However, its slower execution compared to C++ can be a limitation in computationally intensive tasks. The General Graphical Lasso (GGLasso) algorithm in Python's Python R-package is highly efficient and provides stable solutions, but its original Python implementation may suffer from speed limitations. To address this, we developed GGLasso, a new Python version of the package with an integrated C++ implementation of the GGLasso algorithm using the Generalized Conditional Gradient method. This improvement enhances computational performance while retaining the beneficial features of the original package for exploring and visualizing graph structures in Python. We demonstrate the package's capabilities using real-world data sets.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and compared, focusing on the accuracy of solutions and the preservation of invariant measures under transformations. Our analysis yields optimal results for integrating the Euler-Maruyama scheme, demonstrating its ability to accurately solve the Brownian dynamics equation and approximate the target distribution correctly. Furthermore, we propose an enhanced configurational sampling technique, which combines the strengths of multiple existing methods and delivers accurate approximations of the target distribution. In addition, we introduce two innovative approaches, which incorporate the Brownian dynamics sampler into Monte Carlo Markov Chains to efficiently solve problems involving high barriers and rapidly changing parameters. Finally, our proposed methods are demonstrated through applications to the Ising model and the calculation of polarizabilities in DNA base pairs.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when the splash dome closes, an essential aspect of surface seal, are presented in this paper and found to be speed-dependent, lacking universality across different impact speeds. These speeds are measured relative to the sphere's terminal speed. Furthermore, two main mechanisms for film breakdown are identified and observed, an insight not readily apparent due to film dynamics occurring too quickly. These measures of speed are applicable to both hydrodynamic and Wannier surface seal regimes and demonstrate that the relevant physics governing surface seal and splash dome behavior span a broader range than previously thought. This range includes the hydrodynamic regime and water entry speeds for various objects, including spacecraft, projectiles, and bullets.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms emerge as crucial elements in these theories. These $\theta$-terms generate nonlinear connections between axion fields and quadratic gauge field strengths which can be used to break many universal symmetries. If we consider charged states as part of the scenario, additional universal symmetries may be destroyed, yet we found that the $\theta$-terms yield a Witten-like effect that indicates that the range of charged states is composed of an endlessly populated, lattice-like spectrum generated through the monodromy transformation, an element of the boundary near which we established the $\theta$-terms' behavior.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A rapidly growing field in quantum physics is multid particle rabi oscillations, which has a broad spectrum of applications in cutting-edge technology. As a result, research in this area is intensifying. Quantum dots are an ideal platform for investigating multi-particle rabi oscillations due to their small size and long coherence times. This study explores the characteristics of dark exciton giant rabi oscillations in a GaAs quantum dot under an 8T external magnetic field. The "giant" nature of these oscillations is caused by strong driving fields that overcame saturation effects typically seen in dark exciton dynamics. The period of dark exciton oscillations showed a linear increase with the driving field pulse length and did not show any evidence of phase slips. The oscillation period showed a distinct pattern with dark states zero- and one-phonon sidebands. The sidebands are a product of inelastic scattering and allowed for the transfer of dark to bright states through phonon emission and reabsorption processes. The results show the feasibility of dark exciton giant rabi oscillations as a precise measurement tool for controlling and detecting external magnetic field variations.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group, specifically focusing on a square lattice with glide symmetries. By applying a linear Peierls phase, we are able to identify two distinguishable scenarios in which Kleinian behavior occurs. In the first scenario, the hyperbolic nature of the lattice allows us to locate two separate Dirac points that can be moved along specific high-symmetry lines. In the second scenario, we can manipulate the positions of the Dirac points by adjusting an external parameter related to a periodic potential. We also examine several relevant material applications for both scenarios.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state with minimal intensity sends light through a catalytic device, and a detector then identifies a photon at a specific output port, triggering the cancellation of the vacuum state. Due to the distinctively nonclassical characteristics of their underlying components, SPCCSs exhibit superior nonlocality disruption capabilities compared to other single-photon-generated states. Furthermore, we find that conditions for spawning nonlocality and error-free teleportation in the SPCCSs arise in disparate regions of the catalytic device's parameters. Notably, we observe that suitable beam splitters can produce states capable of reliably transporting unknown qubits across nonlocality-deficient linkages. Meanwhile, as catalytic conditions facilitate spawning nonlocality, the corresponding success rates for teleportation improve, offering a unique advantage over conventional setups that utilize single-photon-generated states for nonlocality and teleportation.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that adhere to chemical rules, and employs linear regression in its initial stage. The proposed methodology has been tested through simulations and real-world applications, yielding an accurate predictive model that achieves an R-squared value of 0.95, predicting molecular properties of polymers. Compared to the base model without additional complexity, this new method achieves superior predictive accuracy.

Detecting tumors in the esophagus using CT scans is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning, but it presents challenges due to the lack of clear boundaries in some images, varying tumor sizes and shapes, and the presence of noise and images with incomplete sections. To overcome these difficulties, a new method building upon the U-Net model, known as Dilated Dense Attention Unet (DDAUnet), is proposed for segmenting tumors in CT images. This model has three main components: Dense Unet blocks that capture local features, attention mechanisms that focus on important regions, and dilated convolution blocks that capture long-range dependencies. To test the DDAUnet's performance, it was used to segment tumors in 820 thoracic CT images, and quantitative results show improvements over benchmark methods, including 94.34 hours of segmentation time for 820 images, a Dice score of 0.7955, and a Hausdorff distance of 5.40 mm. These results highlight the effectiveness of the DDAUnet in accurately detecting tumors in esophageal CT images.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly employed to train and assess image description systems, yet their quality is questionable. This study investigates the use of crowd-sourced reference descriptions for evaluating image description technologies. Experiments drawn from the Visual Question Answering (VQA) and Image Captioning datasets reveal that these reference descriptions contain significant errors, as demonstrated by reduced performance in VQA and inflated metrics in image captioning when using manually corrected versions. A set of 50 example pairs, available online, illustrates the range of inaccurate reference descriptions found.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal reflectivity. Recent studies have also considered Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles as potential enhancers for hadron therapy treatments of cancer. To understand the material's electronic behavior, researchers have used theoretical simulations based on first principles. Yet, Ta$_2$O$_5$ has various forms, complicating efforts to identify suitable simulation models. To resolve this issue, researchers utilized statistical methods to determine which Ta$_2$O$_5$ polymorphs share similar structural attributes. Two oxidation states, a triagonal and an octahedral configuration, are found in all identified Ta$_2$O$_5$ polymorphs. By applying statistical analysis to 15 Ta$_2$O$_5$ polymorph structures, researchers discovered that one structure, named Ta$_2$O$_5$-X, has the most similar attributes to other Ta$_2$O$_5$ polymorphs. Further analysis revealed that Ta$_2$O$_5$-X exhibits characteristics akin to the $\delta$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ structure. By applying first-principles simulations to the Ta$_2$O$_5$-X nanoparticle model, researchers determined its minimal energy state, surface features, and electrical properties. The outcomes of these studies provide a solid foundation for interpreting the properties of Ta$_

Previous studies have characterized the significance of geographic mobility among American Reddit users as a catalyst for economic growth and general welfare. This paper expands on the concept of geographic sort behavior by expanding its scope to include the transmission of false information during the 2020 presidential election. As a result of our analysis, which examined more than a million Reddit pages shared on various platforms, including Facebook, Twitter, Google News, and Wikipedia, we found that users who frequently sort content based on their location are more likely to spread unfact-checked misinformation. In addition, we observed a correlation between higher levels of anonymity and the circulation of misinformation. Furthermore, we discovered that sort-based mobility's effect on the propagation of misinformation lessens as the level of anonymity decreases or during peak news cycles when information accuracy is elevated. In addition to its economic implications, our research expands the discussion surrounding false information dynamics by incorporating the impact of online activity mobility.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose is essential. This study examines audio input from humans instructing a robot using Sawyer via spoken language by analyzing three key features: speech duration, tone variation, and speech content. Evaluating these features across four dimensions, it was discovered that instructors frequently use the same vocabulary to describe specific task elements despite varying situations such as task types, audio instructions, and errors encountered during demonstrations. However, differences in speech patterns including duration and inflection are present across these conditions, showing that human speech carries significant, potentially valuable information for enhancing robotic learning through demonstration-based methods.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly difficult to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and incorporating interactions. A promising approach to address this challenge is developed by deriving the time evolution of a complex state within conformal field theory using the equation of motion. This approach reduces the problem to solving the Conformal Group on a real line through a first-order differential equation. A conformally invariant equation is derived to compare the dynamic states' complexity. This equation relies on determining the path integral of e^{-∫γ σ complexification speed ds}. For small perturbations of free theories, this equation can be solved, resulting in calculations of the complexity rate for two-point functions at various conformal points. The invariance of this equation ensures the two-point complexity includes a combination of Bessel functions as an explicit example. The proposed framework yields the universal Casimir complexity for both N=4 Super Yang-Mills and phi^4 theory in two dimensions as further applications.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the text-based output of a conversational system.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are commonly utilized to address SParsity Concern, yet they are hampered by limited domain transferable knowledge and restrictedSParsity Processing capabilities respectively. To overcome these constraints, this work proposes a novel framework called as "Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation" (MSDCR) that integrates both
single-target and dual-target cross-domain recommendation. A comprehensive
preference learning concept is introduced in MSDCR, fusing triplets of
single-target relationships and dualts of dualts from multiple sparse
domains in a unified structure. Furthermore, an adaptive dual gate mechanism,
an enhanced dual-knowledge module, and a multi-objective optimization strategy are designed to refine the model'sSParsity Processing and Transferable Knowledge capabilities. Extensive experiments conducted on three real-world
datasets demonstrate that MSDCR delivers superior results compared to state-of-the-art
single-target and dual-target CDR baselines, demonstrating enhanced performance in addressing bothSParsity Concern and Knowledge issues.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory consumption. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The escalating quantity and quality of MRI data are fueling the rapid progression and customization of medical imaging techniques and related machine learning models. Nevertheless, several issues persist, including parameter generalization concerns and risks associated with poor data quality affecting subsequent analyses and training. A notable instance of generalization problem is QC, where models must effectively generalize to new, unlabelled images. A subset of MRI quality control (QC) methodologies has been hindered by limited data quantities and manual labelling requirements, constraining their customization potential via deep learning techniques due to simulation necessity and high costs. In the context of brain MRIs, we devise QCGeneralizer, a novel framework that identifies high-quality images suitable for lower-performing downstream tasks, thus optimizing data quantities for customized analyses. QCGeneralizer employs a lightweight, yet effective two-stage process comprising an initial, large-scale cluster-based QC method, followed by a more precise deep learning-derived rejection classification. The framework's efficacy is demonstrated through statistical significance in comparing mean segmentations produced using datasets assembled from high-quality versus randomly selected MRIs, as well as its effectiveness in optimizing downstream task performances.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, initially developed to explain and predict the behavior of curious, driven, and socially intelligent animals, has demonstrated success in analyzing and emulating the actions of solitary curious and driven robots. In this study, we take the framework one step further by adapting it to account for the collective behavior of multiple interactive and intelligent creatures exhibiting curiosity and socialization. We focus on a recurring meeting scenario where robots strive to gather at the same location within the shortest possible time. Our results indicate that a small group of robots can efficiently reach a point of rendezvous in a confined environment within 2 to 2.5 times the time it takes to navigate the surrounding area. Additionally, these meetings are likely to occur at more peripheral locations rather than in central areas. Our findings using the Multi-Agent Motivation Dynamics framework provide valuable insights for the design of cooperative location tasks and collaborative activities in complex environments.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes with rising Cm content in the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, and these materials share some key characteristics, rendering them promising for spintronic technology applications.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group to $SU(2) \times U(1)$ and adding new vector fields. These additions include two more families of leptons and various baryons and mesons. The minimum mass for the particles that mediate interactions is set at 320 GeV. The lepton families predicted are likely accessible for experimentation at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The predicted decay patterns result in signatures featuring missing energy and jets of hadronic matter, with specific final states arising from the decay of the lightest quarks in two generations set at 5.4 TeV in LHC experiments.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. However, this connection required modification in relation to the finite unitary group SU_N. In this article, we extend the ordered generating sequences framework to the compact special unitary group. We demonstrate the connection between the standard unitary presentation and this framework, which is comparable to the relationship established by the standard Coxeter presentation for Sn.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. This approach allows us to calculate the integrated galaxy light along the line of sight to each supernova and detect distortions in the properties of foreground galaxies due to gravitational effects. By comparing observed properties with intrinsic distributions, we can infer a measurement of shear for each individual SN Ia. To enhance our data, we employed PSF-matching to minimize artifacts caused by differences in point spread functions. Furthermore, we utilized intrinsic color variations to obtain intrinsic $g-r$ values for the majority of the Pantheon sample. We found no significant signal for lensing effects by individual galaxies and found our results to be consistent with previous research, although with lower precision and a narrower range of effective redshifts. We found that the average shear is non-zero and exhibits the expected behavior with increasing redshift, albeit with somewhat elevated intrinsic scatter compared to theoretical predictions, likely as a result of limitations imposed by SN Ia intrinsic color variations and PDF width, which we estimate have the most significant impact on our final shear estimates. The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high T center densities within the 220nm device layer of Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers, using a process that combines ion implantation and heat treatment. By developing a method to measure spin-dependent optical transitions, we found that high T center densities located near the interface can exhibit ~1 GHz level spin lifetimes for both their electronic and nuclear spins. These results provide a foundation for integrating T center-based quantum devices into integrated photonic circuits.

For our task that considers context, first we create a detector using MSRA 10-1 dataset that can identify objects and their surrounding areas. This special object detection model is based on segmentation models. However, when applied to the TC dataset, the detector fails to accurately locate objects and the associated areas. This in turn impacts the subsequent context-based task. Rather than rectifying the detector, we instead modify the context-related annotations and algorithm to better fit the data's limitations. Instead of treating the detector's output as infallible, we adjust our method to navigate its inaccuracies. Despite the difficulties in accurately defining objects and their associated areas, we manage to make progress on the context-related task by incorporating the problematic detector into our algorithm. This is demonstrated by the improvement in the overall system's overall performance, as shown in the quantitative and qualitative assessments.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$, within the bounded domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $x$ contains the origin with smooth boundary, and for a certain condition $\beta\in[0,2)$; here $m$ denotes a function that belongs to Kirchhoff type, $f_i$ behave like $e^{\beta s^2}$, and there is a function $h_i\in \left(\big(H^1_0(\Omega)\big)^*,\|\cdot\|_*\right)$. By making use of a singular Trudinger-Moser inequality for a small positive value $\varepsilon$ and variational methods, we are able to establish sufficient conditions for a multiplicity of the system's solutions given the given conditions.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic monotone or negative regression property of order one. Notably, our findings for the negative regression property are new contributions to the field, complementing previous results obtained via the positive dependence framework. These findings hold true in a broader context than i.i.d. variables, and are applicable to algorithmic challenges like Boolean matrix factorization and learning parity with threshold.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties. Patients receiving incompatible transplants face a higher risk of transplant rejection, infections, and cancer, and are more likely to lose their transplants. We aim to find the optimal acceptance criteria for patients, taking into consideration the finite time they have, the potential failure of transplants, mortality, sensitivity to immunosuppressive medications, successful organ allocation, and the ethical dilemma of deciding between accepting compatible or incompatible donors. Using optimal stopping theory, we identify the best approach to approving compatible donations and the conditions under which incompatible donations should be accepted. It is found that only highly desensitization-treated patients should be considered for incompatible transplants, and that acceptance should be reserved for patients with the lowest levels of incompatibility. As the risk of incompatibility increases, it becomes more beneficial to approve compatible donations, and we also observe that time limits, organ scarcity, the availability of incompatible donations, and the level of desensitization treatment, all influence the approval criteria in both the short and long term. Furthermore, we observe that the optimal approach to approving low-incompatibility patients may be the same as for those with low levels of compatibility.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical examination of the word2vec model, particularly in its implementation with the Skip-gram learning method. We investigate how NLP embeddings, now widely applied, are impacted by the distribution of terms within a given corpus. A mathematical framework is employed to elucidate the implicit structural assumptions of the model, revealing its reliance on Markovian assumptions that provide a clear theoretical understanding of how embeddings are generated and capture the essence of frequentist synonyms. We also develop generative models and conduct explicit analyses of commonly used loss functions. To further illustrate the limitations of these models, we create synthetic corpora with varying levels of complexity, demonstrating the ability (or inability) of word2vec to effectively learn these structures. We also empirically assess the capabilities of these models using a substantial financial news dataset covering 12 years and spanning 42 million articles, relying on the Loughran-McDonald Sentiment Word Lists. Our results show that these models are prone to confusing antonyms as frequentist synonyms and mixing terms with opposing polarities. Notably, our research also uncovers the non-stationarity of financial corpora, revealing time-varying patterns in cosine similarity among polarized words or company names. Our analysis highlights the entangled mixture of languages and semantics inherent in unsupervised learning datasets, offering valuable insights for subsequent studies in the field.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding the Nash Equilibrium, learning the rationalizable equilibrium (RE) represents another meaningful goal. We note that RE offers a more reliable prediction than the Nash Equilibrium (NE) under the assumption that players eliminate strategies that are unlikely to be chosen, a concept known as rationalizability. We propose a multiagent learning algorithm to find the RE and prove that it converges at a rate of $\O{\frac{\O{pS_a+\sqrt{P}\sum_a \sqrt{S_a}}}{\epsilon\sqrt{T}}}+\epsilon$, where $P$ is the product of the number of actions for each agent, $S_a$ is the number of rows in the payoff matrix for agent $a$, and $T$ is the total number of matrix entries revealed. Furthermore, our method can be used as a black box to develop an alternative convergence proof for the multiagent $Q$-learning method to reach the NE rate of $\O{\frac{\O{pS_a+\sum_a \frac{A_a}{\delta}\log\frac{1}{\delta}}}{\epsilon\sqrt{T}}}+\epsilon$.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs of key properties of the model, particularly its early stages and the phase where the epidemic spreads rapidly. They also found that under certain conditions, there are sharp transitions marked by sudden changes in the sudden changes in the sudden disappearance of epidemics, which are sudden changes in the model's parameters.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurately fitting probability density functions. While aligning the format of the input data is a known issue, it is supplemented by another format discrepancy stemming from differential cross sections. To fit data effectively, cross sections must be normalised to a specific set of probability density functions, and typically a subset of cross sections from distinct sets is used. However, this limits the fitting process to only those sets associated with those specific cross sections. In contrast, this work presents a method to unify the format of data and cross sections by converting them into matched spectra, which resamples both data and cross sections in accordance with kinematic variables, and also incorporates detection efficiencies and other corrections. This approach enables the entire library of differential cross sections to be used simultaneously, providing more information for the fit than traditional methods, and also allows for greater flexibility in applying fits to diverse datasets. While this method has been demonstrated with the MCNN PDF fitting software, it represents a more general framework for PDF fits that can be realised through various implementations.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations. However, the current approach equally values all collected observations, neglecting their varying significance. A more adaptive method, the variance reduction based experience replay framework, selectively leverages the most informative historical data. This approach prioritizes past observations more likely to represent the current target distribution. Theoretical and practical evaluations demonstrate that this method accelerates optimal policy discovery and boosts the effectiveness of state-of-the-art policy optimization methods.

In our analysis of conversational dialogue, we face numerous possible responses 
to any given history, leading us to present the MultiTalk Dataset. This large 
dataset comprises over 320,000 written conversational dialogue sentences, 
maintaining a high degree of complexity (a 10-way branching factor) along with 
60-way branching subtree iterations. Our study on spoken language conversations, 
however, reveals an even more vast potential response space, with branching 
factor and iteration possibilities significantly exceeding those in written text 
conversational dialogue. To effectively navigate this complexity, we propose 
generative models of conversational dialogue that can successfully generate 
multiple simultaneous history branches or entire tree structures, including 
multiple interconnected nodes. Our research highlights the importance of 
conversational dialogue complexity in the creation of more realistic and 
intricate tree-based structures, along with an expanded benchmark for 
conversational dialogue evaluation, and provides a novel approach to 
question-answering on highly-branching tree-based structures via the use of 
complexity-aware generative models of natural language.

We introduce MG-GLAM, a computational tool developed to rapidly create comprehensive N-body simulations for various cosmological theories, specifically modified gravity models. This program builds upon the existing GLAM code and incorporates an advanced multigrid method to solve the non-linear equations characteristic of modified gravity theories, resulting in highly efficient simulations. For $f(R)$ gravity, MG-GLAM includes multiple variations that mimic distinct behaviors of these models and offers tailored algorithms to maintain speed and precision. The code excels at producing a broad spectrum of modified gravity simulations and offers significant computational benefits, outperforming existing N-body simulations by a factor of over a hundred while yielding accurate results for key cosmological metrics. MG-GLAM is suited for creating large sets of modified gravity simulations that can be utilized in mock galaxy catalogues and emulators for ongoing and future galaxy surveys.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pairing of subdomains of the complex plane and associated Gaussian free fields under conformal equivalence. Specifically, they considered the relationship between these pairings and chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution. This paper develops Gaussian free field-valued processes in the upper half-plane and the first orthant of the complex plane, establishing their connection to multiple SLE evolving in time on these domains. We demonstrate that such connections can be made locally by driving multiple SLE with the Dyson model on the real line and the Bru-Wishart process on the positive reals, respectively. Ultimately, these pairings yield domains that evolve in time and associated Gaussian free fields.

MediaWiki's 'WorkingWiki' is an open-source extension that converts a wiki
into a sophisticated collaborative platform for developing high-quality manuscripts
and software projects. Originally developed at McMaster University's theoretical
biology lab, WorkingWiki enables multiple users to work together on a range of
tasks by utilizing command-line tools to translate raw'source code' into desired outputs.
Its features cater specifically to programmers and researchers who use languages
like R, Python, and C, and it boasts specialized tools for seamless LaTeX editing.
By integrating features from collaborative editors, development environments,
version control systems, and publishing platforms, WorkingWiki unlocks the
full potential of wiki-based collaboration, and its customizable'makefiles'
and modular architecture enable users to tailor and repurpose its functionality.

This study undertakes a linear analysis of weakly turbulent jet flames subjected to acoustic fluctuations to develop a predictive model for flame instability. We utilized the Active Flame method, which allows for real-time calculation of control necessary to prevent thermoacoustic oscillations and accurately replicate experimentally observed jet flame behavior. By employing this approach, we incorporated key features such as flow velocity, heat release patterns, and geometry into our model. We further simplified our model through linearization, focusing on predicting flame instability. We examined the interaction between the flow's intrinsic instability and external acoustic waves, and developed an efficient method for solving the Rayleigh equation. Furthermore, we applied the Green's function technique to address the Orr-Sommerfeld equation and incorporated its solution into our model. Our model's accuracy was validated against existing literature and it was discovered that acoustic waves can either amplify or counteract the intrinsic instability of the jet, with a new, distinct pattern of vortex shedding emerging in the downstream direction as a unique feature of jet flame instability in this context.

We investigate the neutrinoless double beta decay driven by an extremely light dark matter field interacting with neutrinos, particularly focusing on the impact when this interaction breaches the lepton number, which directly leads to a significant influence on the $0
u eta eta$ decay, even when neutrino masses are very small. Since the ultralight dark matter can be adequately modeled as a classical field, this analysis incorporates the effects of the dark matter spectrum on the $0
u eta eta$ decay probability. Furthermore, we establish new constraints on the interaction strength between the neutrinos and the dark matter based on the observed $0
u eta eta$ decay duration. Additionally, an examination of the cosmological consequences of the dark matter-neutrino interaction reveals that the same framework is applicable to analyze the constraints imposed by the early universe's particle production, the structure of the cosmic microwave background, and the formation of large-scale structures in the universe. An intersection of these diverse $0
u eta eta$ decay duration and cosmological constraints results in a narrow, permissible range for the relevant parameters of the theory, which may potentially allow the future $0
u eta eta$ experiments to detect signals attributable to ultralight dark matter.

Nonlocal gravity theory is a classical generalization of Einstein's gravity theory. Based on an analogy with nonlocal electrodynamics, this new model involves a history-dependent relation that can be confirmed through data. The purpose of this paper is to modify nonlocal gravity theory so that the nonlocal aspect relates directly to observable properties, similar to the approach in nonlocal electrodynamics. The reformulated theory results in a constitutive relation identical to one proposed recently by Puetzfeld, Obukhov, and Hehl. The nonlocal gravity theory can be applied to show that de Sitter spacetime does not meet the theory's requirements.

Understanding how genomic elements affect specific traits through genome-wide association studies remains complex due to the sheer number of available annotations. We've developed a statistical method to pinpoint relevant genomic elements, based on multivariate patterns across the entire genome in various model traits. This method uses factor analysis to reduce data dimensionality and employs Bayesian techniques for precise element assessment. When applied to 18 human traits, our results reveal trait-specific differentiation among genomic elements, with evidence found in elements affecting blood cell counts, lipid levels, and certain diseases in mice and humans. Additionally, we found that some species-specific elements may play an underappreciated role in human traits.

This paper discusses recent findings from the LHC involving small systems studied
by the ALICE, ATLAS and CMS collaborations. Due to the growing significance
of QCD in small systems, particularly in situations with high multiplicity, not
all pertinent research can be covered within this report. It primarily examines
measurements focusing on collective behavior in small systems and new results on
strangeness enhancement observed in proton-proton interactions. It is essential to
note that many notable findings have been excluded from the discussion presented
here.

Observations of some variable X-ray sources within the Milky Way's center that have shown no outbursts in over a decade have led some researchers to suggest a significant number of them are neutron stars within an active star formation region, potentially indicating high levels of activity in this area. In the context of accretion discs around these sources, even a minimal level of residual gas can sustain considerable brightness levels. Nevertheless, many astronomers contend that these sources are likely X-ray binaries and should exhibit recurrent bursts within relatively short time frames. By examining a sample of well-documented neutron star transients in the Milky Way, the calculated average time for renewed bursts falls within the range of 30 to 60 years. This range is somewhat lower than previously estimated values but also comes with substantial uncertainty. Consequently, the total energy emitted by the sources over extended periods can easily account for what is observed. Unfortunately, due to significant uncertainty, it is currently challenging to accurately predict the total energy emitted by these sources in the Milky Way's center.

THz radiation enables the precise stimulation of vibrational frequencies in molecules and crystals, leading to the introduction of inertial influences on electrons. By drawing a comparison to classical mechanics, where circular motion generates Coriolis and centrifugal forces, analogous effects arise, specifically spin-rotation coupling, centrifugal field coupling, and the interplay of these forces with the spin-orbit and the redshift of energy levels. These effects can persist for a few picoseconds following the initial stimulation, and potentially amplifying their magnitude could make this approach a promising means of controlling localized quantum states and chemical reaction barriers via vibration.

Improving neural conversational agents' ability to produce diverse, engaging responses in casual conversations is a challenge. To tackle this issue, this paper introduces two significant innovations. Firstly, it proposes a new assessment metric that employs Natural Language Inference to gauge the semantic variety of responses generated by the model in a conversation turn, utilizing a robust and easily accessible benchmark. Unlike existing methods, this metric leverages natural language understanding capabilities and has the ability to capture semantic diversity effectively. Furthermore, it demonstrates that integrating an inhibitor mechanism into the conversational model during training leads to increased model performance, as evidenced by decreased language and semantic repetition, in addition to maintaining high response quality and various other characteristics. This approach is demonstration- free and does not involve any additional turn constraints or the use of auxiliary models. Moreover, it provides evidence that the generated responses are both factually accurate and diverse in a range of topics.

The occurrence of sustainable hydrogen burning in very low-mass stars might be impacted by rotation due to the addition of centrifugal force and potential break-up caused by rapid spinning. Computer simulations model rotating low-mass stars with the capability for sustained nuclear reactions, considering a range of rotation rates, rather than slow rotation alone. Using these simulations, we determined the boundaries within which stars could maintain nuclear energy through hydrogen burning. These boundaries varied based on angular momentum. However, above a certain threshold (approximately 8.85 x 10^48 erg s) the boundaries broke into two distinct branches, resulting from objects losing mass and experiencing extreme spin. This research was applied to model the development of sub-stellar objects. Two possible scenarios were modeled: one with external forces gradually slowing the star, mainly controlled by spin-down time, and another where the star spins out of control, ultimately shedding mass and shrinking.

The technique of amplitude analysis in hadron decay studies is quite effective, 
However, this analysis faces a major challenge in addressing instrumental influences 
such as fluctuations in background levels and selection efficiency across different 
multidimensional kinematic scenarios.  This article will review traditional methods 
used for calculating efficiency and background probability and discuss the application 
of two techniques specifically density estimation using Gaussian processes and 
artificial neural networks. Although widely adopted in other contexts, these methods 
have not been heavily employed for amplitude analyses. The article also introduces 
new applications for these models, such as leveraging sidebands to determine the 
density of background in multiple dimensions, as well as more comprehensive density 
estimation utilizing artificial neural networks.

A new model based on a comprehensive expression for radiation energy has been proposed, and it effectively elucidates the dynamics of afterglows in multiple contexts, including relativistic, non-relativistic phases and fireball radiations with radiative and adiabatic components.

Bipartite graphs depicting connections between distinct groups of objects have numerous practical applications, and their visualization often takes the form of a 2-tier layout where corresponding entities are aligned horizontally across two parallel lines, connected by lines representing relationships between them. The task of reducing edge crossings within these visualizations can be computationally intensive, yet might not always guarantee sufficiently low crossings levels to maintain the visualization's clarity. In contrast, an approach has been developed to remove edge crossings by splitting specific nodes, targeting the minimum number required to yield an edge-free (planar) drawing. The question of determining if an edge-free representation exists after breaking at most a specified number of nodes remains tractable in relation to that number.

This paper will present our approach to optimizing bipedal robot walking assisted by thrusters using a closed-loop feedback system. By assuming that supervisory controllers are under-utilized, we will develop and examine models comparing fixed and adaptive jet-assist parameter settings during the walk cycle. To analyze efficiency, robustness, and smoothness, we will employ appropriate metrics to compare constant jet-assist strategies with variable, responsive adjustments to the jet-valves. Demonstrating these comparisons, an experimental setup featuring a seven-degree-of-freedom legged prototype will be utilized.

Becker-Denef-Lipschitz first observed in 1979 that over finite fields $k$, the total residue map $\text{res}$ from Laurent series to $k$ is expressible in a specific language, provided $t$ is included as a parameter. This discovery motivated further research into the properties of a specific mathematical theory related to valued fields. In the course of these investigations, the authors proved that this theory does not have a certain desirable feature and demonstrated that, for infinite fields $k$, the associated power series fields cannot be computationally decided. This, in turn, led to an analogous undecidability conclusion for a specific complex-valued field of power series.

In order to enhance side-channel attacks, this research introduces a new technique, HyperDegrade, which incorporates previous methods and employs simultaneous multithreading architectures. The novel approach focuses on utilizing multiple threads to accelerate a context-switching-based frequency degradation attack at the operating system level. The developed framework includes two main components: a context-switching frequency degradation engine and an application-specific frequency degradation engine. The former was tested using both synthetic and real-world applications, which demonstrated an average degradation of 2.6 GHz across different systems within a time frame of 12 seconds. The latter was devised to introduce a more advanced degradation of applications' execution speeds. The effectiveness of the frequency degradation technique was further evaluated using the TM4e side-channel attack, which showed an improved correlation coefficient of 0.24 on average and extended the acceptable attack time window by two orders of magnitude. The resulting application-specific frequency degradation was found to be significantly more effective than previous methods, which typically achieved a maximum degradation of 1 GHz. The research also provides an extensive analysis of influencing factors, including CPU microarchitectures, thread configurations, and system settings, to further refine the effectiveness of the frequency degradation technique.

A localized alteration in knot diagrams is referred to as an unknotting operation. It can be demonstrated that any knot diagram can be converted into a trivial unknot through a sequence of unknitting operations specific to the type of classical or welded knot theory being considered. Previously identified examples of such operations include crossing changes, smooth and cusp sharp switches, interchanges, and conversions. This study introduces a new operation, the "Neckelose," distinct from prior operations, and explores its characteristics in both classical and welded theories. Additionally, the paper investigates the impact of the Neckelose on various knot invariants, including the Jones, Kauffman, and Chebychev-Kodama invariants for classical theory, and the signed Kauffman invariants for the welded theory.

We've demonstrated that combining the 1-cocycle of a long knot's space with Fox-Hatcher 1-cycles through integration produces a specific Vassiliev invariant, having a precise order of three. This discovery builds on a preceding finding by the second listed author, proving that I(X) integrated over the Fox-Hatcher 1-cycles of a long knot's space generates an invariant with a vascular number up to three. However, by creating a counterexample, it was established that the vascular number of I(X) can exceed three at most. Furthermore, this inductive approach using I(X) and the Fox-Hatcher 1-cycles yields a basis for the space of Vassiliev invariants up to a given order, in this case, five. But through additional procedures similar to those in the indective approach, it was also proven that the space of Vassiliev invariants up to order five can be spanned by the following combinations: the second order of I(X) and the third order of the fox-hatcher 1-cycles, or alternatively, by second and fourth orders of invariants derived from I(X) and the fox-hatcher 1-cules.

In cooperative systems with multiple agents, coordination enables tasks to be performed more efficiently by sharing information about actions. This study focuses on a coordination challenge where agents must share insights on an optimal task selection strategy, based on input variables that differ between them. The ideal strategy is represented by a concise, structured mathematical pattern that each agent can store and use to make informed decisions. We examined various methods for communicating the pattern, finding that the simplest approach using basic values works best when there's a significant difference in energy costs for storage and communication. Furthermore, by analyzing the costs, our findings identify the conditions under which the chosen pattern allows tasks to be completed energetically feasible. The proposed solution was successfully applied to determine optimal tasks in real-world scenarios involving an actual drone fleet.

Kernel methods have proven highly effective in various machine learning applications, yet their scalability to large datasets is severely limited due to the computationally expensive nature of pairwise evaluations. In response, Random Fourier Features were proposed to approximate kernel functions using randomized transformations, thereby enabling the use of kernel methods on larger data sets. While widely adopted, this method has significant drawbacks, notably requiring an unnecessarily large number of features, directly proportional to the size of the dataset, in order to achieve satisfactory results comparable to traditional kernel-based methods. In order to circumvent these limitations and efficiently process large datasets, this paper introduces an alternative method of kernel approximation that leverages insights specific to the underlying data and offers both feature dimensionality reduction and performance enhancements. We test and evaluate this novel method against a range of competitors, including RFF, orthogonal random features, and the Nyström method.

In our study, we demonstrated how both a group that operates on a set in a recurring manner and a diagonal group are effectively incorporated into the wreath products under their combined representation, using the Cartesian Decomposition technique.

This research paper examines conformally flat hypersurfaces of n-dimensional space (n is 4 or higher) within a hypersphere of n+2 dimensions. We start by classifying and describing these conformally flat hypersurfaces when they have constant M\"obius curvature under specific transformations. Next, we prove that a compact hypersurface with this constant M\"obius curvature, denoted R, is specifically equal to $(n-1)(n-2)r^2$ for values of r less than 1. Furthermore, if this hypersurface is compact, we establish that it is topologically equivalent to a torus defined by the union of a circle with a radius of $\sqrt{1-r^2}$ and a hypersphere with a radius of r in the higher-dimensional space.

A new method of efficient wireless communication is proposed in a novel SWIPT system, enabling faster and more sustainable mobile data networks. The system, utilizing energy-harvesting technology from access points without the need for a splitter, allocates part of the frequency spectrum for information transmission and the remaining for energy capture. To analyze performance improvements, an optimization problem was created that maximizes energy gain and maintains a minimum data rate in a multi-user OFDMA network. Next, the model was refined to investigate resource allocation strategies in SWIPT systems, focusing on optimizing transmission parameters to minimize harvested energy requirements in an OFDMA-based IoT system. Finally, the paper explores potential applications and challenges of this novel SWIPT technology and examines various existing techniques for managing data transmission and energy capture.

Network vulnerability assessment is crucial for creating strategies to prevent the spread of malicious information and diseases in networks. Researchers often study network immunization, but traditional approaches typically focus on broad measures, such as network criticality and component size. In contrast, this paper delves into a micro-level analysis, where the removal of individual nodes and their associated edges during an attack is examined in detail. Based on percolation theory, the authors derive the statistical behavior of nodes and components affected by an cascading failure, specifically within the context of an isolated component in Cayley tree networks.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of measurement and signal loss in optical recycling systems. Overcoming this constraint is critical for identifying gravitational waves generated by binary neutron star mergers. We present the concept of the sloshing Sagnac interferometer topology, an innovative variation of the Michelson design where the end mirrors are optically linked to form an additional resonating cavity. By transforming the detector into a system with multiple coupled cavities, this design outperforms the conventional Michelson setup with optical recycling, offering improved optical isolation and reduced photon loss. Under ideal conditions where the outer cavity is highly tuned, theoretical models suggest that the quantum limitation threshold can be met even with moderate power redistribution between the two interferometers. We also examined the efficiency of this design in comparison to other advanced topologies using specific detector parameters analogous to LIGO.

Recent large-scale MIMO systems are considered an exciting development, capable of providing rapid data transfer in crowded environments. As a result of their substantial size, MIMO arrays are subject to space-based disruptions and varying ranges that affect how data is perceived by nearby devices and limit the area they can cover. By taking into account these range limitations and limit data access to only devices within a specific detection area, researchers have created the Random Access method for extreme-scale MIMO communications and calculated its performance under various conditions and delay settings. In order to assess the system's performance in terms of data transfer, they also developed an enhanced scheduling technique to manage limited data transfer issues. By considering the limited areas where devices can communicate, researchers have used machine learning methods to identify patterns and create access control rules to maximize data transfer efficiency. However, due to varying shapes and sizes of limited areas, existing control rules are difficult to apply and require significant adjustments. As a solution, we have devised a new access control technique called the Hybrid MIMO Scheme that combines the best aspects of existing methods to improve data transfer efficiency while considering the limited areas where devices can communicate. In order to assess the best aspect of each method, we have used reinforcement learning techniques to train the MIMO Scheme to optimize data transfer efficiency while considering the limited areas where devices can communicate. Through extensive simulations, we have shown that the MIMO Scheme achieves higher data transfer efficiency than existing methods by accurately combining the best aspects of each method to minimize limited data access issues.

Recent high-resolution observations at millimeter and submillimeter frequencies have revealed that planetary disks exhibit complex patterns caused by small-scale turbulence and large-scale features, including T-shaped and U-shaped structures and spiral arms. The instability caused by vertical shear in the same disks may enhance small-scale turbulence and T-shaped structures while diminishing internal gaps and internal shocks as a result of enhanced small-scale scattering. These predictions hold true during a specific phase when vertical shear reaches a particular wavenumber range suitable for enhancing the spiral pattern. The scenario in which particles are concentrated at the perimeter of the disk's midplane results in internal shocks that could be observed. The SMBHO-3.8 model predicts that the 3.8 GHz gap will be obscured by T-shaped structures or internal shocks in the dust continuum. We suggest that observing such features around this frequency with next-generation radio telescopes like the Chinese Radio Telescope (CRT) and next-generation European Very Large Array (EVLA) could help confirm the origin of the 3.8 GHz gap.

A question remains regarding the secondary component of GW190814 - whether it's a neutron star or a black hole of minimal mass. Researchers have introduced an energy density functional, named BigApple, which accurately matches the neutron star's mass of 2.60 solar masses and is in line with GW190814's data. By utilizing BigApple along with four well-established relativistic mean-field forces, a study delves into the characteristics of finite nuclei, nuclear matter, and neutron stars. The predicted properties of finite nuclei and calculated quantities of nuclear matter align well with empirical and experimental values, demonstrating the BigApple parameter set's reliability in describing the equation of state. Notably, BigApple successfully accounts for GW190814's neutron star, as the minimum mass for a neutron star under this model matches the 2.86 solar masses reported in GW190814.

This research focuses on creating resilient Molmer-Sorensen gates using trapped ions arranged in a line, incorporating Gaussian amplitude modulation and a consistent laser frequency. We chose to use this frequency method due to its suitability for rapid and complex quantum operations between photon interactions. To develop a robust frequency method, we introduced two measures of performance - gate fidelity in response to motion frequency distribution and an average field leakage risk for ions. Both measures are influenced by the modulation depth, which we aimed to minimize while keeping the risk below an acceptable threshold. By examining many configurations of Gaussian frequency distributions and employing an artificial neural network, we discovered that minimizing modulation does not always result in better gate fidelity, and thus we established an optimization strategy to achieve the highest possible fidelity at an acceptable field leakage risk. We applied this approach in a concrete example using Gaussian amplitude modulation, achieving an $N$-independent residual error of $10^{-4}$ and an $N$-independent threshold of $055$ needed to reach a residual error of $10^{-4}$ after accounting for non-resolved sideband imperfections.

Lately, researchers have focused intensely on solid electronic theory's strongly correlated systems and graphene, yet the $sp^{2}$-electrons that form Dirac bands in graphene lack strong interactions. Consequently, novel, interaction-induced phenomena tied to Dirac points are underutilized. We propose GaCu$_{3}$(OH)$_{6}$Cl$_{2}$ as a new material where Dirac electrons are paired with strong interactions and frustrated magnetism. Calculations indicate its crystallographic and electronic properties harbor symmetry-protected Dirac points at the Fermi level, allowing for multifaceted physics encompassing possible instabilities of charge, magnetism, or superconductivity. By merging various methods to assess its many-body behavior, researchers have observed potential transitions to Mott-Hubbard, magnetic, or charge ordering states in GaCu$_{3}$(OH)$_{6}$Cl$_{2}$, along with an exotic, dynamically generated anti-ferromagnetic spin state and the emergence of d-wave pairing and unconventional superconductivity in this unique material.

Researchers explored the capabilities of the NA62 experiment at CERN to enhance restrictions on a specific parameter in the Standard Model, specifically related to the interaction between a particular lepton and heavy neutral particles. By analyzing the process of $K^+ \to \pi^0 e^+ N$, they determined the present limit can be set at $2\times 10^{-6}$ for a particular lepton interaction with masses ranging from 125 to 144 MeV, a region that current production searches lack in depth. Combining existing data with optimized detection tools or improved photon rejection techniques can significantly narrow this limit.
